nodes.name: Cleaning and Hydrothermal synthesis of Ni(OH)2/NF
nodes.procedure: Prior to its usage, NF was cleaned following a standard procedure. The cleaned NF, together with 30 mL of 0.02 M NiSO4·6H2O solution, was transferred into a Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and then heated at 160 °C for 5 h.

nodes.name: Anodic electrooxidation of NiO/NF
nodes.procedure: The anodic electrooxidation treatment was carried out at ambient temperature using a standard three-electrode cell with the NF-supported sample as the working electrode, graphite plates as counter electrode and Ag/AgCl (with 3.0 M KCl) as reference electrode. The electrooxidation operation was conducted in an aqueous solution of varied concentrations of KF and FeSO4 at 5∼20 mA·cm^{-2} for a duration ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 h. The thus-prepared catalyst was carefully cleaned following the routine procedure.

nodes.name: Drop-casting RuO2/NF reference
nodes.procedure: 5 mg of powdery RuO2 (99.9%) and 60 μL of 5 wt% Nafion solution were first ultrasonically dispersed in 1 mL of deionized water/ethanol mixture (4:1 v/v) for 1 h to form a homogeneous ink. 500 μL of the ink was then drop-cast onto the cleaned NF, and the resulting sample was finally dried at ambient temperature.

nodes.description: OER LSV polarization curves in O2-saturated 1.0 M KOH (general testing condition for all catalysts)
nodes.source_text: In the present study, we conducted all electrochemical measurements on a CHI 660E workstation at room temperature using a three-electrode setup as described above. All electrochemical potentials were calibrated versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE). The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) polarization curves were measured in an ${ \sf O } _ { 2 }$ -saturated 1.0 M KOH solution over a potential range of $1 . 2 3 \sim 1 . 6 3$ V versus RHE at a scan rate of $1 \mathsf { m } \mathsf { V } \mathsf { s } ^ { - 1 }$ with $9 5 \%$ iR compensation. ... Table S3. ... Ni1-xFexOOH/NiO/NF: 225 mV ... Ni1-xFexO(OH)1-yFy/NiO/NF: 186 mV
EIS measurements were performed over a frequency range of $0 . 1 \mathsf { H z }$ to 100 kHz at open circuit potential (OCP).

The double-layer capacitances (CDL)of the samples were determined by performing cyclic voltammetry (CV) in a non-Faradaic region at scan rates ranging from 10 to $6 0 \mathrm { m } \mathsf { V } \mathsf { s } ^ { - 1 }$ .
The Faradaic efficiency was evaluated based on the collected ${ \sf O } _ { 2 }$ and ${ \sf H } _ { 2 }$ volumes at the anode and cathode sides, respectively.
